title: Chelsea's secret payments: the record fine
checked: PL (16 Mar 2026): record £10.75m incl. £750k youth fine, 9-month academy registration ban, 1-year first-team ban suspended 2 years, undisclosed payments 2011-2018 by third parties to players, unregistered agents and others, more than £47m (Sky £47.5m, Insider Sport £47m: said 'more than forty-seven'), self-reported after the 2022 takeover, no points; previous record West Ham £5.5m 2007 (Citizen/AP, Irish Times, Sky, ESPN). UEFA €10m settlement 28 Jul 2023 for incomplete financial information (Soccerway/Flashscore, earlier InsideWorldFootball). FA: 74 breaches of Rule E1.2, £10m fine; first commission -6 pts suspended to 30 Jun 2027; appeal (31 Jul 2026) set the points aside, imposed a two-window registration ban suspended to 30 Jun 2027, a further breach brings an immediate one-year ban (Express & Star/PA, Irish News, eNCA). Drogba's 88th-minute header from Mata's corner, 1-1, won 4-3 on pens, 19 May 2012 (Football Italia, Boston Globe). Trophies 2011-18: CL 2012, EL 2013, PL 2015 and 2017 (club honours). The £20m 'without self-report' figure has one source only: left out. 32 players (one source): left out.

lines.text: More than forty-seven million pounds in secret payments. Made in Chelsea's greatest years.
Under Roman Abramovich, Chelsea won almost everything. In 2012, even the Champions League.
lines.say: Under Roman Abrahmovitch, Chelsea won almost everything. In twenty twelve, even the Champions League.

lines.text: Munich, the eighty-eighth minute. Mata's corner. Drogba's head.
lines.say: Munich, the eighty-eighth minute. Mahta's corner. Drogba's head.

lines.text: But behind the trophies, money was moving where nobody could see it.
In 2022, new owners bought the club. Going through the books, they found the payments, and reported them.
lines.say: In twenty twenty-two, new owners bought the club. Going through the books, they found the payments, and reported them.

lines.text: UEFA moved first. Ten million euros, for incomplete financial information.
lines.say: Yooayfah moved first. Ten million euros, for incomplete financial information.

scene.headline: Chelsea agree €10m settlement with UEFA
scene.standfirst: European football's governing body says the club submitted incomplete financial information under its previous owner.

lines.text: Then the Premier League's findings. Payments to players, to unregistered agents, and to others. Never declared.
March 2026: a ten point seven five million pound fine. The biggest in Premier League history.
lines.say: March, twenty twenty-six: a ten point seven five million pound fine. The biggest in Premier League history.

scene.title: The biggest fines ever
scene.note: The previous record stood for 19 years

lines.text: Plus a nine-month ban on signing academy players, and a one-year transfer ban, suspended for two years.
But no points. Chelsea had owned up, and reported it themselves.
Then the FA. Seventy-four breaches of its rules on agents.
The first ruling: six points off, suspended. Chelsea appealed.
On appeal, the points were scrapped. Instead, a two-window transfer ban, hanging over them until June 2027.
lines.say: On appeal, the points were scrapped. Instead, a two-window transfer ban, hanging over them until June, twenty twenty-seven.

scene.headline: Points deduction removed after Chelsea appeal
scene.standfirst: The £10m fine stands. A ban on registering players for two transfer windows is suspended until 30 June 2027.

lines.text: Break the rules again before then, and the doors shut for a whole year.
A record fine, for the club's greatest years.
Follow for more, and play Road to Ballon d'Or.
